           CYPRIPEDIUM PUBESCENS

         Yellow Lady's Slipper

        (CYPRIPEDIUM)


The skin symptoms correspond to those of poisoning by Rhus, for which it
        has been found an efficient antidote. Nervousness in children; from teething and intestinal
        troubles. Debility after gout.   Hydrocephaloid   symptoms,
        result of long, exhausting diarrhœa.   Sleeplessness  .
        Cerebral hyperasthesia in young children often the result of overstimulation of brain.



Head.--  Child cries out at night; is wakeful and begins to
        laugh and play. Headaches of elderly people and during climacteric.



Relationship.--  Compare:   Ambra; Kali
        brom; Scutellar; Valerian; Ignat  . Skin relatives:   Grindelia;
        Anacard  .



Dose.--  Tincture, to sixth attenuation. For Poison Oak, 5 drops
        of tincture per dose, also locally.
